title: Local US officials’ views on the impacts and governance of AI: Evidence from 2022 and 2023 survey waves
abstract: This paper presents a survey of local US policymakers’ views on the future impact and regulation of AI, capturing changes in attitudes following the release of ChatGPT and the subsequent surge in public awareness of AI.

sections.title: The Core Insight
sections.content:
Imagine you're a local policymaker, trying to make sense of AI's impact on your community. You're not alone - our survey reveals that most local policymakers anticipate AI will create significant societal risks over the next decades, including increased surveillance, misinformation, and political polarization.

But what does this mean for you? Let's dive in and explore the key findings.

config.title: Expected AI Impacts on Local Communities

sections.title: How It Works
sections.content:
Our survey asked local policymakers about their expectations of AI's future impact and their attitudes towards specific regulatory policies. We found that most policymakers think AI will be positive for US innovation and transportation/infrastructure, but have more measured views about its economic impacts.

So, what do these findings mean for AI governance?

config.title: Expected AI Impacts on US Economy and Infrastructure

sections.title: Benchmark Results
sections.content:
We compared the results of our survey across two waves, 2022 and 2023. We found that support for AI regulation increased significantly, from 56% in 2022 to 74% in 2023, with increases across party lines.

What does this mean for the future of AI governance?

config.title: Support for AI Regulation Over Time

sections.title: Why This Matters
sections.content:
Our study highlights the need for capacity-building initiatives and bi-partisan coordination to mitigate policy fragmentation and build a cohesive framework for AI governance in the US.

So, what can we do to address these challenges?

sections.title: Key Innovations
sections.content:
Our survey provides insight into the perspectives of local policymakers, key players in shaping state and federal AI legislation. We found that Democrats show greater support for a broad range of AI policies, while Republicans are more skeptical.

What are the implications of these findings?

config.title: Party Affiliation and AI Policy Support

sections.title: What Came Next
sections.content:
Our study contributes to understanding the perspectives of local policymakers on AI's future impact and regulation. Future research could build on our findings by exploring the specific areas where policymakers may feel least informed or prepared, such as the technical aspects of AI or its economic implications.

What's next for AI governance?
